description: Wears 37th Fighter Interceptor Squadron markings; serial read off the airframe in Rod Bearden's 2017 photo log and matched by militaryaircrafthistorian; 51-3064 sits inside the FY51 F-86D block from which all F-86L conversions were drawn
Carries wingtip fuel tanks in place of the F-89D rocket pods; 52-2129 sits inside the FY52 F-89D block that supplied the F-89J conversions; two independent photo logs agree
Painted in USAF Thunderbirds demonstration team markings; 54-2145 lies inside the FY54 F-100D block 54-2091 to 54-2304
Serial lies inside the FY51 T-33A production block; confirmed on the airframe in 2017
Wears VA-37 markings; BuNo 157506 lies inside the A-7E block 157435 to 157595
Dual-control conversion of the F-101B interceptor; 56-0246 lies inside the FY56 F-101B block

Built by Republic Aviation at Farmingdale New York and delivered 29 January 1962 per the park's own interpretive marker; retired from service November 1981; year_built taken from that delivery date not from the FY61 order year; serial lies inside the FY61 F-105D block 61-0041 to 61-0223

Built at St Louis and delivered to the USAF 19 August 1970 per the park marker; served 363rd TRW Shaw AFB 1971; 26th TRW Zweibrucken 1973; 18th TFW Kadena 1987; 460th TRG Taegu 1989; painted in 18th TFW Kadena markings; 69-0372 lies inside the FY69 RF-4C block

One of six Kestrels supplied to the United States for the tripartite evaluation and afterwards flown by NASA Langley as NASA 520; militaryaircrafthistorian's serial 64-18268 is rejected because it falls outside the 64-18262 to 64-18267 block; identity 64-18266 agreed by Wikipedia AirHistory.net and dated Flickr logs
aliases: XV6A; XS692; NASA 520; N520NA; P.1127; Kestrel; XV6

description: Army intermediate range ballistic missile; park marker states it was built by Chrysler Corporation with a Rocketdyne liquid-fuelled engine of roughly 150000 lb thrust and a range of 1500 miles
Surface-to-air missile; both booster and upper stage are displayed; current interpretive marker in place after the 2024 refurbishment
Army surface-to-surface ballistic missile; marked M-2 Corporal on the park signage
Booster of the type used at Wallops to test the Mercury capsule escape system; displayed with a Mercury boilerplate capsule
